newsitem.title: MEXICO: Credibility of Mexico prosecutors takes fresh knock.
newsitem.headline: Credibility of Mexico prosecutors takes fresh knock.

text.p: The battered credibility of Mexican prosecutors took a fresh knock on Friday when a newspaper said there were serious inaccuracies in a key press statement and a judge complained of sloppy investigations.

President Ernesto Zedillo has made respect for the law a key plank of his administration, but his efforts so far to improve the poor image of Mexican justice have been hampered by problems at the Attorney General's office.
Last month Zedillo fired Attorney-General Antonio Lozano for what aides said was gross incompetence. But the latest embarrassment to the office has come under its new chief, Jorge Madrazo.
The Attorney-General's office (PGR) claimed a big success on Monday night, saying police and soldiers had raided a top drug lord's family wedding and arrested more than 25 people.

But sources at the office said on Friday all but five of those arrested had been set free and none of the suspects still behind bars was of any importance in the Juarez drug cartel led by Amado Carrillo Fuentes.
And a leading newspaper, Reforma, said the Attorney-General's office had given false information about several key aspects of the raid on the wedding of Carrillo Fuentes's sister, Aurora.
"The information given by the PGR on the case is incorrect in at least three central points," Reforma said.

The newspaper said the PGR wrongly claimed three airplanes used to fly guests to the wedding had been seized. It also wrongly said their pilots were arrested and it falsely alleged that the pilots had not filed flight plans, Reforma said.

Asked about the allegations, a PGR spokeswoman said: "The press bulletin was based on the information which we had at the time. I think this is bad faith by someone." She did not deny that the information was inaccurate.

Newspapers earlier this week quoted residents of the town of Navolato in the northwestern state of Sinaloa where the wedding was held as saying Amado Carrillo Fuentes attended the lavish ceremony but escaped before police arrived.
"Police were waiting to catch him there when he appeared at the wedding," commentator Miguel Angel Granados said. "But a timely warning allowed the fish to slip the net."

Mexico's war on drugs suffered another blow this week when a judge acquitted accused top cocaine lord Hector "The Blonde" Palma on drugs charges, saying there was insufficient evidence to convict him.

The PGR attacked the decision, hinting that corruption might have been behind the acquittal. But that criticism boomeranged when the judge said the main reason he could not convict was that the PGR had not supplied adequate evidence.

Judge Amado Lopez Morales said the only evidence the PGR supplied of drug trafficking was the statements of agents who arrested Palma and confessions of supposed accomplices. There was no firm proof of trafficking, he claimed.
